newsitem.title: USA: SAIC agrees to buy Bellcore.
newsitem.headline: SAIC agrees to buy Bellcore.

text.p: Defence contractor Science Applications International Corp. said Thursday it agreed to buy Bell Communications Research Inc., the research and engineering arm of the seven regional Bell phone companies, which is also known as Bellcore.
The terms of the deal were not disclosed, but a report in September said Morristown, N.J.-based Bellcore would be sold to SAIC for about $700 million.

Bellcore's board said early last year that its owners were considering selling the company because of changing developments in the telecommunications industry and the seven owners' diverging strategies and business plans.
"Bellcore and SAIC are well positioned for the future," J. Robert Beyster, chairman of San Diego-based SAIC, said in a statement.

"We envision serving new markets where our two companies can combine their considerable skills. These include large software projects, advanced network designs, secure networks, Internet technologies, wireless communications and other advances in telecommunications software systems and technology," Beyster said.
The deal is expected to be finalised late next year after Bellcore's owners obtain regulatory approval, the companies said.

Bellcore, formed in 1984 as a research and engineering company supporting its seven owners, provides communications software, engineering and consulting services. It has 5,600 employees and annual revenues exceeding $1 billion.
It is owned by the regional Bell operating companies -- Ameritech Corp., Bell Atlantic Corp., BellSouth Corp., NYNEX Corp., Pacific Telesis Group, SBC Communications and U S West Inc.

Employee-owned SAIC provides high-technology products and services to government and private industry. With annual revenues exceeding $2.2 billion, SAIC and its subsidiaries have 22,000 employees in more than 475 locations worldwide.
